presets.name: Deck options
presets.description: Packages of study options shared by decks: daily limits, learning steps, desired retention.

presets.heading: Deck options
presets.intro: Set how many new cards and reviews a deck shows each day, and when a card you got wrong comes back.
presets.none: No presets yet: every deck uses the defaults.
presets.decks_none: No deck uses this preset yet. Pick one below.

field.name: Name
field.fsrs_hint: Leave it empty to use defaults that suit most people. The optimizer in Statistics → Planning works these out from your review history and writes them here.

presets.pick: Choose a preset on the left to see its options.
presets.none_hint: If some decks should work differently (e.g. more new cards a day for an exam deck), create a preset and use it for those decks.
presets.decks_intro: When a deck gets a preset, its subdecks use it too (unless they have their own).

desc.name: Only shown in this list; it does not change how you study.
desc.new_per_day: How many new (never seen) cards to show each day. More means faster progress, but more reviews on the following days too.
desc.reviews_per_day: The most reviews asked in one day. At the limit, that day's reviews stop.
desc.desired_retention: The chance you still remember a card when it comes back (70%–99%).
desc.learning_steps: How many minutes apart you see a new card at first. In minutes, separated by spaces.
desc.relearning_steps: How many minutes apart you see a card again after you forget it (answer “Again”).
desc.new_order: New cards in the order they were added, or mixed.
desc.review_order: The order waiting reviews come in. “Weakest memory first” brings forward the cards you are about to forget.
desc.bury_siblings: Cards made from the same note (e.g. a reverse card) don't come one after another on the same day.
desc.maximum_interval_days: The longest time between two reviews of a card (1–36500 days).

presets.delete_desc: Decks using it fall back to their parent deck's preset or the defaults. Undo is available.
presets.used_by: {n, plural, one {# deck uses this preset: everything you change here affects it.} other {# decks use this preset: everything you change here affects all of them.}}
presets.used_by_none: No deck uses this preset yet; you can use it for a deck below.
presets.on_defaults: {n, plural, one {# deck uses no preset: it runs on the defaults.} other {# decks use no preset: they run on the defaults.}}
presets.unsaved_shared: You have unsaved changes. Saving affects {n} decks.
presets.advanced_summary: Card order, related cards, maximum interval and FSRS parameters. Most people never touch these.

how.title: What is a preset?
how.what: A preset is one set of deck options you can use for several decks at once: how many new cards a day, how many reviews, when a card you got wrong comes back.
how.inherit: A deck uses its own preset; if it has none, its parent deck's; if that has none either, the defaults.
how.shared: Changing a preset changes every deck that uses it. To make just one deck different, copy the preset and use the copy for that deck.

section.daily_desc: The most you will study in one day. Once a limit is reached, that day's cards are done.
section.order_desc: The order cards come in and how far apart they can get.
section.fsrs_desc: Numbers that tune the scheduler (FSRS) to your memory. Not typed by hand.

example.new_per_day: {n} → at most {n} new words are asked each day; the rest wait for the next days.
example.reviews_per_day: {n} → after {n} reviews, the rest wait until tomorrow.
example.desired_retention: {pct} → the aim is that you remember about {n} of every 100 cards. Raise it and cards come back more often.
example.learning: {steps} → a new card is asked again after these gaps; once you know it at the last step it moves to daily reviews.
example.learning_none: No steps → a new card moves to daily reviews right after your first answer.
example.relearning: {steps} → a card you forgot is asked again after these gaps, then goes back to daily reviews.
example.relearning_none: No steps → a card you forgot is simply scheduled for tomorrow or later.
example.maximum_interval_days: {span} → even a card you know very well is asked again within this time.
example.bury_siblings: If a word has both an “English → Turkish” and a “Turkish → English” card, once one comes up today the other waits until tomorrow.

pace.title: How many cards a day?
pace.intro: Pick how many new words you see each day and how firmly you want to remember them. At the top you see how many minutes a day that takes.
pace.empty: Make a deck and add a few words first; then you pick here how many you see each day.
pace.curve_label: Minutes a day: today ~{from}, in two months ~{to}
pace.new_label: How many new words a day?
pace.new_desc: Words you have never seen. More means faster progress, but a few days later more reviews too.
pace.new_effect_on: The {n} new words waiting are done by {date}.
pace.new_effect_later: {n} new words are waiting; at this pace they are not done within two months.
pace.new_effect_none: No new words left to start: you only review.
pace.new_effect_zero: No new words come; you only review.
pace.reviews_label: At most how many reviews a day?
pace.reviews_desc: Once you reach it, the day's remaining reviews wait until tomorrow.
pace.reviews_effect: At this pace you get ~{n} cards a day in {weeks} weeks.
pace.retention_label: How firmly do you want to remember?
pace.retention_desc: The chance you still remember a card when it comes back. Stricter = more reviews.
pace.scope: {count, plural, one {This pace applies to: {decks}.} other {This pace applies to # decks: {decks}.}}
pace.scope_new: “{deck}” uses the defaults for now. Your first change opens a settings package of its own for it.
